Name: Sara Newberry
Badge: Teacher as Researcher: Cultivating Literacy Routines
Looking back on this inquiry cycle, what did you learn about your teaching and your students that you might not have noticed otherwise? How did engaging in this teacher-research process shape or shift your thinking about your classroom practice?:

I did not realize until this inquiry cycle that my students are exceptional at determining deeper meanings! Until now, their answers had been mostly superficial, and I had trouble getting them to analyze text as they read. However, the Say-Mean-Matter strategy, in particular, prompted them to provide incredible dissections of the texts we analyzed, showing that my delivery was the issue. I've tried multiple strategies in the past to get students to quote, analyze, and explain, and they never got it until now. My students actually loved it!

Engaging in this teacher-research process helped push me to try new strategies that usually would have gotten forgotten in a notebook somewhere. I'm very thankful I tried them, and I plan to incorporate all three of them in my curriculum. I also intend to alter many of my repeat lessons to incorporate these strategies that promote deeper thought and more meaningful discussions.

What new questions or next steps are you leaving this module with? How might you continue to explore or build on this inquiry in your future teaching?:

I plan to expand on my use of the Say-Mean-Matter strategy. My end goal is for students to have this mindset while they read everything - from the Bible to social media. To do so, I plan to facilitate this activity frequently, particularly while reading informational texts. I think this will make them more successful, educated adults, as well as help them in college when conducting research!
